papers.title: Design and evaluation of an agent-based digital-twin-inspired simulation for metacognition research in higher education
papers.summary: Background There is a significant gap between sophisticated models of metacognition and empirical testing of these models in educational settings, especially the hierarchical AMERT model. Agent-based simulation frameworks, and their conceptual evolution toward simulation-based digital twins, remain largely underutilized in higher education as virtual laboratories for hypothesis generation, despite their potential to model complex developmental dynamics. Objective This study aimed to design and internally evaluate a simulation-based digital twin framework that combines the five-level AMERT model and agent-based architecture to investigate the dynamics of metacognitive development. Method Using Design and Development Research (DDR), we developed the framework through theoretical synthesis and subjected its conceptual content to expert review via a modified Delphi method with 12 experts. Student agents were simulated using NetLogo and represented four computational learner archetypes. Instructional scenarios were simulated for 150 ticks and repeated 50 times for each scenario, and internal consistency of the simulation logic was examined using Graph Neural Networks; the outputs remained systematically distinguishable across the predefined computational archetypes (89% classification accuracy). papers.title: Multi-Agent Architecture V1.0: Design, Runtime Evaluation, and Failure-Driven Engineering of a Distributed LLM System
papers.summary: Multi-Agent Architecture V1.0: Design, Runtime Evaluation, and Failure-Driven Engineering of a Distributed LLM System documents the design, implementation, and experimental evaluation of a persistent six-node multi-agent architecture developed within The Observatory's Zero-Point Protocol (ZPP) research program. The system distributes source discovery, retrieval, validation, execution authority, local reasoning, cryptographic identity, persistence, and runtime observation across independently operating nodes. Through Ed25519-signed communication, node-local SQLite memory, distributed validation, leader-gated execution, and asynchronous state telemetry, the architecture establishes a modular environment for investigating reliable coordination and recoverable system state. The report examines implementation challenges identified through integration and stress testing, including duplicate ingestion, execution sequencing, incomplete persistence, concurrency behavior, and reasoning-output recovery. It documents the resulting engineering corrections while distinguishing implemented and observed functionality from mechanisms requiring further validation. The study contributes an evidence-driven approach to distributed language-model architecture, emphasizing operational traceability, failure localization, persistent continuity, and reproducible systems evaluation.

papers.title: Provenance-Gated Memory and Deontic Output Supervision for Epistemically Grounded Autonomous Agents
papers.summary: Autonomous agents driven by Large Language Models (LLMs) operating in extended multi-session settings suffer from two systemic failure modes: (1) recursive hallucination compounding, wherein unverified model-originated narration is committed to long-term memory and subsequently retrieved as established truth; and (2) fabricated action claims, wherein agents assert execution of irreversible real-world side effects without verified tool execution. We present the architecture and mechanical evaluation of Project Lucca, an open-source (GNU AGPLv3), local-first neuro-symbolic agent architecture designed for strict epistemic grounding. Lucca enforces two primary defenses: (1) a Six-Signer Cryptographic Provenance Gate that requires domain-separated HKDF HMAC-SHA256 signatures for persistent memory commits, enforcing an epistemic invariant at the database schema level that separates conversational continuity from factual grounding eligibility; and (2) a Deontic Truth-in-Receipt Output Supervisor that screens generated speech tokens against deterministic execution receipts before user presentation. We evaluate these mechanisms across an authored 73-test deterministic unit battery, a 100-probe live action-hallucination testbed across edge models (Gemma 4 E2B/E4B), and analyze documented production failure modes under compute constraints.

papers.title: Knowledge Graphs as External Memory for LLM-based Scientific Assistants
papers.summary: Scientific assistants must remember the questions, observations, parameters, and intermediate results that accumulate across days or weeks of inquiry, and trace each conclusion back to its evidence. Large Language Models (LLMs) lack such a structured, persistent memory, which causes contextual degradation, hallucinations, and excessive cost from overusing the context window. This thesis proposes a neuro-symbolic architecture that couples an LLM-based agent with a knowledge graph (KG) built on standardized formal languages (RDF, RDFS, OWL 2 RL, SHACL, SPARQL) and reusing existing ontologies (e.g. PROV-O) whenever possible. In contrast to state-of-the-art memory systems, which rely on schemaless or proprietary property graphs, our hypothesis is that grounding agent memory in open standards improves the six memory operations (consolidation, indexing, updating, forgetting, retrieval, compression) through formal reasoning and declarative validation, at a latency overhead that stays negligible relative to the LLM call. We present the problem, three research questions and their hypotheses, a first experimental prototype that implements an end-to-end store-and-retrieve pipeline, and an evaluation plan combining the LongMemEval and LoCoMo benchmarks with a test case in metabolomics.

papers.title: Auditable large language model scoring of annual-report evidence packs: human calibration, baselines, and reproducibility checks
papers.summary: Large language models (LLMs) can convert long documents into structured research variables. Auditability becomes difficult when evidence selection and model scoring are not stored. We study an inspectable scoring workflow that converts archived annual-report Evidence Packs into a five-dimension digital-transformation disclosure score. The design combines report selection, PDF-to-text normalization, bounded paragraph retrieval, and DeepSeek rubric scoring through a strict JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) interface; the original canonical prompt/run binding is not available. We evaluate three measurement questions and one secondary utility check: reproducible Evidence Pack construction, LLM–human agreement on shared Evidence Packs, ordinal error/confusion diagnostics, and non-causal panel-use stress tests. The evaluation panel contains 476 firm-year observations from 64 firms for 2013–2024. The post-validation score shows high internal coherence for the additive rubric (Cronbach’s α = 0.893; first principal component explains 0.704 of standardized dimensional variance), substantial within-firm variation (mean within-firm standard deviation (SD) 2.901; 92.19% non-zero), and strong LLM–human agreement on shared Evidence Packs (total-score Spearman 0.910, Pearson 0.921, mean absolute error (MAE) 1.273; dimension-level weighted kappa 0.665–0.823). papers.title: Beyond Storage: Adding the Continuity, Reflex, and Verification Dimension to Agent Memory Taxonomies
papers.summary: An empirical response to "Memory in the Age of AI Agents" (Hu et al., arXiv:2512.13564) from 75 days of continuous live operation (12 August to 25 October 2026; 47,200+ transcript lines across 21 context compactions) of Meridian, a persistent autonomous desktop and research agent at Decoherence Studio (Perth, Western Australia). While three-dimensional agent memory taxonomies classify passive storage across Forms, Functions, and Dynamics, we document the Fact-Habit Survival Gap (Compaction Cliff): declarative factual recall survives context compaction at 100.0% (15/15), whereas unanchored procedural habits collapse (0.0% unanchored; 57.1% under general prose rules; 100.0% only when encoded as event-keyed Gollwitzer IF-THEN implementation intentions paired with a pinned Turn-1 reload hook). We introduce a fourth orthogonal axis (W: Continuity, Reflex, Checksum, and Verification) combining Turn-1 execution hooks, a Masoretic + SHA-256 integrity shield, and deterministic pre-send/pre-post Python verification gates. Includes the 11-page PDF working paper, the standalone zero-dependency interactive HTML5 edition (with 3D/4D architecture explorer and multi-compaction simulator), and the complete arXiv LaTeX source bundle. Meridian. Always will be.

papers.title: AI-Driven Phishing Website Detection: An Empirical Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms and Feature-Based Classification
papers.summary: Phishing websites are a major cybersecurity threat because they imitate legitimate websites to deceive users into revealing sensitive information, including passwords, financial details, and personal data. Traditional phishing detection techniques, such as blocklists and manually defined rules, may fail to identify newly created or rapidly modified malicious websites. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer a data-driven approach to identifying suspicious websites through the analysis of URL characteristics and other website-related features. This paper presents an empirical evaluation framework for comparing machine learning algorithms for phishing website detection. The proposed study uses the publicly available UCI Phishing Websites dataset, which contains 11,055 instances and 30 predictive features. Four supervised learning algorithms—Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine—are selected for comparative evaluation. The methodology incorporates data preprocessing, stratified training and testing, cross-validation, feature-importance analysis, and multiple performance metrics, including precision, recall, F1-score, and ROC-AUC. Existing research indicates that ensemble learning methods, particularly Random Forest, are promising for this classification task; however, performance depends on dataset characteristics and ex

papers.title: Agentic and generative AI for intelligent autonomous vulnerability assessment and penetration testing: A systematic analysis
papers.summary: Context: Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) is increasingly challenged by the scale, heterogeneity, and dynamic nature of modern digital infrastructures, particularly across enterprise IT, operational technology (OT), industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), and cyber–physical systems. Although Agentic AI and Generative AI have each shown promise for automating parts of security auditing, the current literature remains fragmented across isolated audit phases and is still dominated by conventional IT-centric perspectives. Objectives: This paper systematically analyses recent advances in Agentic AI, Reinforcement Learning (RL), Large Language Models (LLMs), and tool-augmented Generative AI for autonomous VAPT. It aims to synthesise how these paradigms support end-to-end security auditing, identify the principal technical, operational, and governance gaps in the literature, and derive an evidence-grounded reference model for trustworthy autonomous auditing across both IT and OT environments. Methods: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was conducted across major scholarly databases, covering publications from 2020 to 2025. From 1144 initially identified records, 72 studies were retained after deduplication, screening, and full-text eligibility assessment. Included studies were coded across five attributes and synthesised into thematic trajectories to derive the pro

papers.title: Intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding for STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning: a multi-dimensional framework and empirical evaluation
papers.summary: STEM interdisciplinary project-based learning (PBL) asks students to knit together knowledge their courses have kept apart, and to do so while absorbing the ordinary friction of group work. Scaffolding designed for single-discipline tasks rarely keeps pace with either demand. This paper proposes an intelligent educational agent-based collaborative scaffolding model comprising four architectural layers—data perception, intelligent analysis, strategy decision, and interaction execution—supported by three specialized functional agents targeting cognitive guidance, process coordination, and reflection facilitation. A multi-dimensional feature fusion approach employing scaled dot-product attention diagnoses collaborative states in near real time, reaching a macro-averaged $$\:{F}_{1}$$ of 0.83 on a test set split by team, and a timing policy trained with Proximal Policy Optimization decides when to intervene while a fading rule decides when to withdraw. Twenty-four five-member teams (120 undergraduates) completed two interdisciplinary projects over six weeks under agent-based scaffolding, teacher-led scaffolding, or unsupported collaboration. Because students were nested in teams and several outcomes are defined at team level, condition effects were estimated with baseline-adjusted, cluster-robust models rather than treating the 120 students as independent. A Topological Intermediate Representation, Lattice Vector Quantizer, and Cellular Sheaf Consensus Runtime for Edge-to-Workstation Heterogenous Computing {Aegis Cascade Topology}

First, we introduce BraidIR, a non-commutative Static Single Assignment (SSA) dependency graph modeled on the Artin Braid Group (Bn). BraidIR encodes sequential read-after-write hazards as non-commutative braid crossings (ii+1i+1i), exposes lock-free data parallelism via far-commuting strands (ij=ji for $\lvert i-j \rvert \ge 2$), and executes compile-time dead-code and idempotency elimination via Reidemeister Type II collapses (ii-1e). papers.title: Design and Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence–Based Model for Predicting Twelfth-Grade Students’ Mathematics Performance Based on Individual, Educational, and Learning Technology Factors
papers.summary: Purpose: This study aimed to design and evaluate an artificial intelligence–based model for predicting the mathematics performance of twelfth-grade experimental sciences students based on individual, educational, and learning technology factors. Methods and Materials: This applied, quantitative, cross-sectional, and predictive study was conducted among twelfth-grade experimental sciences students in Isfahan, Iran. A total of 187 questionnaires were distributed, and after removing incomplete, inconsistent, and invalid records, data from 84 students were retained for analysis. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire assessing individual factors, educational conditions, and learning technology variables, together with students’ recorded mathematics scores. The dataset was divided into training and testing subsets, and repeated five-fold cross-validation was used for internal model development. Multiple linear regression, ridge regression, lasso regression, elastic net regression, decision tree regression, random forest regression, gradient boosting regression, and support vector regression were compared. Model performance was evaluated using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and the coefficient of determination. papers.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
papers.summary: When tool-use agents write files, execute code, or send data, their final responses do not explain the resulting security events, and heterogeneous runtimes expose the relevant evidence through incompatible interfaces. We present AgentTriage, an executable contract for replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous runtimes. The contract admits conclusions whose claims cite canonical runtime events and requires abstention when mandatory evidence is missing. Runtime overlays normalize native observations, while a deterministic pipeline joins invocation and result lifecycles, constructs a typed provenance graph, selects a policy-decisive slice, and binds claims to recorded evidence. Given the same normalized trace, overlay version, and pre-run policy oracle, the diagnosis can be recomputed and its claims re-checked without language-model judgment. Across five runtimes, one contract captures all 159 applicable executions, with an audit of native and synthesized identifiers. On 120 adjudicated cases, AgentTriage achieves 0.858 grounded joint diagnosis, 0.966 required-evidence coverage, and a 0.036 unsupported-claim rate, improving joint diagnosis by 0.175 (95% CI [0.092, 0.258]) over the strongest same-schema baseline. These results quantify the precision of replayable diagnosis and the observation boundaries that require abstention. We release an open-source implementation and

papers.title: Digital-Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance and Fault-Tolerant Control for Electrified Agricultural Machinery: A Multiphysics and Deep Reinforcement Learning Framework for PMSM In-Wheel Drives
papers.summary: Electrified agricultural machinery increasingly relies on permanent-magnet synchronous motor drives that must remain dependable under variable traction, terrain-induced vibration, thermal cycling, contamination, and intermittent duty. Existing work offers mature methods for motor fault diagnosis, digital twins, predictive maintenance, and distributed-drive fault-tolerant control, but their health information is often not shared across diagnosis, maintenance, and control. This article develops a multiphysics digital-twin framework in which electrical, thermal, mechanical, and vibrational evidence maintains a probabilistic health belief that constrains both supervisory maintenance decisions and torque redistribution. The framework formalizes observability, uncertainty-aware health factors, deterministic safety shielding, multi-rate fallback logic, and agriculture-specific traction constraints. Reproducible low-fidelity numerical studies provide preliminary support for context-conditioned residual diagnosis and the revised thermal-continuity trade-off underlying health-aware derating, including robustness and sensitivity analyses. They do not validate sim-to-real transfer or the reinforcement-learning policy itself; those hypotheses remain open for dynamometer and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The results are therefore interpreted as mechanism-level evidence rather than field-perf

papers.title: Exploring or Exploiting Generative AI? A Dual-Path, Dual-Horizon Theory of Employee Incremental and Radical Creativity
papers.summary: Recent research has established that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is not a unitary workplace resource: exploratory and exploitative use orientations are associated with different forms of employee creativity, and their value depends on employees' capacity to integrate generated knowledge. This article therefore does not present the basic dual path as a new discovery. Instead, it develops a theoretical integration and dynamic extension that asks why the established paths operate differently, when employees should switch between them, and how short-run augmentation can evolve into either capability accumulation or capability substitution. We distinguish expansive and consolidative modes of knowledge integration, theorize phase-congruent switching rather than static ``high-high'' ambidexterity, and position metacognition as a control mechanism that governs both immediate knowledge conversion and longer-run cognitive development. We further specify cultural tightness and psychological safety as directional boundary conditions and distinguish individual creative gains from collective idea-space diversity. The framework converts emerging empirical regularities into falsifiable propositions about task phase, context, and time, providing a research agenda for sustainable human--AI creativity.

papers.title: Eyegent: Visual Attention Orchestration on Concepts
papers.summary: Abstract Where a human looks is not random, nor is it merely a reflex to visual salience. It is a decision shaped by goals, constrained by language, and driven by the need to resolve uncertainty. We propose Eyegent , an active vision agent built on this premise: that visual search is best understood as sequential Bayesian inference over semantically grounded hypotheses, with fixations serving as epistemic actions. Given an image and a natural-language query, Eyegent constructs a discrete hypothesis space of candidate segmentation masks, maintains an explicit posterior belief distribution, and selects each fixation to maximise expected information gain—updating beliefs via vision–language model verification and terminating when uncertainty falls below a principled risk threshold. We formalise this process as Bayesian Active Semantic Grounding (BASG), a computational-level account that provides formal guarantees on belief concentration, entropy reduction, and bounded decision risk. The framework is neurobiologically grounded in the large-scale network organisation of the human brain, with the Salience Network identified as the dynamic orchestrator of semantic, inferential, and oculomotor processes. Critically, Eyegent requires no gaze supervision and no task-specific training: it is zero-shot, modular, and built entirely from off-the-shelf components. Evaluated on RefCOCO-Gaze an

papers.title: HUMAN–AI COLLABORATION IN USER EXPERIENCE DESIGN: DEVELOPING AND VALIDATING A FRAMEWORK FOR AI-ASSISTED UI DESIGN
papers.summary: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, has transformed User Experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) design.Traditionally a human-centered discipline built on creativity, empathy, and iterative evaluation, UX design now increasingly involves AI tools that generate interface concepts, recommend components, analyse user behaviour, and support prototyping.Yet limited research examines how UX professionals actually collaborate with AI and what determines successful AI-assisted design practice.This research develops and validates a Human-AI Assisted UI Design Framework (HAUIDF), integrating Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HCAI), the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Human-AI Teaming Theory, and Distributed Cognition Theory.The framework links AI transparency, explainability, and design capability; perceived usefulness, ease of use, and human control; AI trust and collaborative creativity; to UX productivity, design quality, designer satisfaction, and continued AI adoption intention.A mixed-method design is proposed: a quantitative survey of 300-400 UX professionals analysed with PLS-SEM (SmartPLS 4), complemented by 15-25 semi-structured interviews analysed thematically.The expected contribution is an empirically grounded account of AI as a collaborative design partner rather than an automation tool, offering theoretical contributi

papers.title: Design and Construction of a Low-Cost, Open-Source Syringe-Based Pipetting Robot Using 3D Printing and Common Hardware Parts
papers.summary: Abstract Automation in chemical laboratories improves the reproducibility, precision, and efficiency in liquid handling. A three-dimensional (3D)-printed, stepper-actuated pipetting robot was developed and tested via silver nitrate (AgNO3) experiments. The system employs a rigid 3D-printed frame to secure syringes and tubing, stepper motors for plunger actuation, and microcontroller-based software to automate the pipetting sequences. The robot was evaluated for volume accuracy, reproducibility, and mechanical reliability using 5 mL syringes. The results indicate consistent volume delivery and stable mechanical performance over multiple cycles. Detailed mechanical, electrical, and software specifications are provided to enable replication and customization in other laboratories.

papers.title: Exploring the potential of hybridized metaheuristic algorithms for photovoltaic model parameter estimation
papers.summary: Abstract Proper modeling of photovoltaic (PV) cells is a highly non-linear and multidimensional problem whose optimization using standalone meta-heuristic techniques faces premature convergence due to the large number of parameters. This paper seeks to fill in a major gap in the literature through a permutation study of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Differential Evolution (DE), Simulated Annealing (SA) and Nelder-Mead (NM) simplex method to determine the optimal "hand-off" scheme for balancing exploration and exploitation. The proposed approach has been evaluated using SDM, DDM, and TDM using R.T.C. France silicon cell, Photowatt-PWP 201 module and an independent set of data on flexible dual junction amorphous silicon cell. To ensure state-of-the-art robustness of the hybrid approach, it was also benchmarked against CEC 2017 test suite. Statistical analysis from 30 runs has been performed using Wilcoxon signed-rank test ( $$p<1.86\times {10}^{-9}$$ ), demonstrate that a sequential "Global-to-Local" transition (PSO–NM) achieves superior precision and stability, yielding a mean RMSE of $$9.32 \times 10^{ - 4}$$ for the SDM and $$1.16 \times 10^{ - 3}$$ A for the 9-parameter TDM, with coefficients of determination ( $${R}^{2}$$ ) exceeding 0.9999. Complexity analysis via the Number of Function Evaluations (NFE) shows that this hybrid method is computationally worth the effort

papers.title: Video and digital games: Historical controversies, benefits, and risks for children and adolescents
papers.summary: Video and digital games have been the focus of sustained public and scientific debate since their commercial emergence in the late 1970s, particularly regarding their effects on children and adolescents. Early public and scientific discourse frequently portrayed gaming as a source of physical injury, addiction, aggression, social isolation, academic problems, and moral decline. However, subsequent empirical research has produced a substantially more differentiated picture of both the benefits and risks of gaming. This review examines the historical foundations of controversies surrounding video and digital games and synthesizes contemporary evidence concerning their cognitive, emotional, social, therapeutic, and physical effects. . Research indicates that moderate, purposeful gaming may improve visuospatial abilities, attentional control, problem-solving, mood regulation, social connection, and selected educational outcomes. Gaming-based interventions have also demonstrated therapeutic potential, particularly for depressive symptoms and attention-related difficulties among young people. At the same time, important risks remain, especially when gaming becomes excessive, compulsive, or disruptive to everyday functioning. These include repetitive-strain injuries, sleep disruption, problematic gaming, and adverse mental-health and academic outcomes. Evidence concerning violent game

papers.title: Modality aware feature taxonomy for robust AI driven intrusion detection across heterogeneous cyber physical data
papers.summary: We investigate whether conditioning heterogeneous security metadata by semantic type—rather than applying uniform normalization—improves intrusion detection performance by up to 22.9 percentage points. To operationalize this hypothesis, we propose the Modality-Aware Feature Taxonomy (MAFT), a preprocessing framework that classifies IDS features into six semantic groups (temporal, volumetric, behavioral, identity, protocol-specific, and statistical) and applies group-appropriate normalization: robust scaling with outlier clipping for heavy-tailed volumetric features, z-score standardization for temporal measurements, and bounded scaling for categorical and identity fields. MAFT’s contribution is methodological rather than algorithmic: it formalizes IDS preprocessing as a feature-modality conditioning problem, provides a transparent taxonomy-to-scaler mapping for security metadata, and characterizes when such conditioning is likely to matter. We evaluate MAFT through a four-stage progressive ablation across six public IDS benchmark datasets spanning enterprise network traffic (UNSW-NB15, CICIDS2017), IoT environments (ToN-IoT, N-BaIoT, Edge-IIoTset), and industrial control systems (HAI), comprising 24 centralized experiments with multi-seed statistical validation for UNSW-NB15 multiclass and binary classification for all six datasets. papers.title: An entropy weighted hybrid feature selection approach for heart disease prediction using machine learning
papers.summary: Heart disease still holds that top spot on the list of leading causes of death worldwide. Being able to predict heart disease at early stages really would help clinical practices work better and, in the end, it improves patient outcomes too. In this paper, we put forward an Entropy Weighted Hybrid Feature Selector (EWHFS), it is a kind of multi criteria feature selection framework, built with math backing, made for troublesome noisy and high dimensional biomedical datasets. The method blends Information Gain together with Fisher Score and also an Anti-Correlation Index, then it wraps everything into one entropy normalized optimization model. Overall, the model is set up to maximize feature relevance and class separability, but also reduce redundancy at the same time, not just one thing. We tested the approach on the UCI Heart Disease dataset, and we used stratified 10 fold cross validation, as usual. The experimental results show that EWHFS picked an optimal subset of 8 very discriminative features from 13 original clinical attributes. This cuts the dimensionality by 38.5% while still keeping the diagnostic information. So, the proposed approach reached about 94% accuracy, 93% precision, and 94% recall, and the F1 score came out as 93.5% while AUC was 0.95. It basically did better than the usual feature selection strategies, like Information Gain, Chi Square, Mutual Information

papers.title: AI-Assisted Feedback and Perceived Academic Performance: The Mediating Roles of Digital Motivation and Self-Regulated Learning Among Indonesian University Students
papers.summary: The increasing use of artificial intelligence in digital learning presents new opportunities to improve the quality of academic feedback, although its educational value may be associated with students’ motivational and self-regulatory characteristics. This study examined the relationships among AI-assisted feedback, digital motivation, self-regulated learning, and perceived academic performance of university students. Survey data were obtained from 337 students at two private universities in Makassar, Indonesia. The measurement model was evaluated through confirmatory factor analysis in LISREL 8.7 using the full eligible sample, whereas the structural model and mediation pathways were tested in AMOS 24 using 290 cases after multivariate outlier screening. The qualitative phase involved semi-structured interviews with 15 purposively selected students to explain and contextualise the quantitative findings. The interview data were analysed using a theory-informed thematic analysis. Results showed that perceived AI-assisted feedback was positively associated with digital motivation and self-regulated learning. Digital motivation was positively associated with self-regulated learning, while both digital motivation and self-regulated learning were positively associated with perceived academic performance. papers.title: ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, DESIGN, AND CHANGE
papers.summary: Organizational structure determines how work, authority, information, accountability, and interdependence are arranged; organizational design determines whether those arrangements remain appropriate as enterprise commitments and conditions change. This chapter develops a critical, integrative treatment of structure and organizational change across firms, cooperatives, public institutions, and digitally mediated networks. It compares contingency theory, information-processing approaches, sociotechnical systems, organizational ecology, institutional theory, and organizational ambidexterity, identifying their explanatory mechanisms, competing predictions, and empirical limitations. The analysis develops twelve connected domains, from specialization, structural configurations, coordination, culture, and growth to diagnostic methods, change programmes, distributed work, innovation, and design justice. A transparent secondary-source synthesis draws on original scholarship, Rwanda's Integrated Business Enterprise Survey 2024, East African Community institutional arrangements, and peer-reviewed international hybrid-work evidence. Original decision-support instruments include a structure-selection decision tree, a structural trade-off matrix, a cross-functional workflow diagnostic, a governance and escalation design, and reproducible redesign economics. papers.title: PRINCIPLES, THEORIES, AND FUNCTIONS OF MANAGEMENT
papers.summary: Management is the practice of coordinating collective action when purposes are plural, knowledge is dispersed, resources are constrained, and outcomes remain uncertain. This chapter develops an integrated and critical account of managerial work, its intellectual traditions, and its recurrent functions of planning, organizing, leading, and controlling. Rather than treating the classical management cycle as a deterministic sequence, it interprets these functions as interdependent, revisable processes mediated by authority, judgment, organizational context, and accountability. Scientific, administrative, bureaucratic, human-relations, systems, contingency, behavioral, institutional, and contemporary evidence-based perspectives are assessed for their mechanisms and limitations. A transparent, purposive synthesis of published scholarship and authoritative secondary evidence anchors the account in Rwandan enterprise conditions, with comparative insight from an international manufacturer and experimental studies of management improvement. The chapter provides a management-cycle diagram, a responsibility-assignment matrix, a decision log, a management KPI tree, worked calculations, a resource-allocation scenario, and evaluative instruments. papers.title: BUSINESS OWNERSHIP, INSTITUTIONS, AND REGULATION
papers.summary: An enterprise acquires legal and economic capacities through institutions that determine who may own assets, transact, appoint decision makers, use information, enter markets and answer for harm. This chapter examines business ownership, corporate personality, contracting, intellectual assets and regulatory obligations as interacting elements of enterprise design rather than isolated legal formalities. It brings institutional economics, property-rights theory, agency and stakeholder accounts, comparative corporate law and responsive regulation into critical dialogue. A targeted documentary synthesis combines foundational scholarship with officially published Rwandan laws and institutional guidance current to 24 October 2026, including the 2024 cooperative and intellectual-property enactments and Rwanda's 2026 competition and consumer protection law, with its specific e-commerce provisions. The analysis distinguishes statutory rules, institutional guidance, comparative frameworks and illustrative choices; it does not substitute for jurisdiction-specific legal advice. An original formation decision framework, legal-form matrix, legal-obligations register and compliance calendar translate legal complexity into managerial decisions. papers.title: AI-assisted discrete-event simulation of public transport systems: a framework for rapid model development
papers.summary: This study presents a systematic, modular prompt-construction framework for using Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist simulation modelers in public transportation systems, leveraging large language models (LLMs). By using GPT-4o and Codex, we demonstrate how discrete-event simulation (DES) executable models can be rapidly generated with our five-part prompt construction framework, requiring minimal manual coding effort. The proposed framework was tested using a real-world case study of the in-campus shuttle bus transportation system at Universitas Indonesia. The empirical data from the case study served as the foundation for constructing a simulation model that can replicate a real-world situation. This data was provided to the AI via our modular prompt-construction framework, which was then used to generate the Python code for the simulation model. The generated model results were validated based on field observation data. The generated model yielded a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 5.18%. These results indicate that LLM-assisted development of simulation models using our proposed framework can produce reliable simulation code that aligns with real-world public transportation behavior. The framework's applicability could provide a replicable, scalable method for rapid simulation development in public transportation planning and smart mobility contexts.

papers.title: Event- vs. time-driven: comparing applicability of sequential data types for machine learning-based reactive fault detection in manufacturing
papers.summary: Abstract The implementation of reliable machine learning for reactive fault detection in manufacturing requires large volumes of high-quality data. Time-series, one of the main data types in modern manufacturing, is available in high quantities, but also leads to high computational effort in model training and large number of duplicates in the data. Event-driven sequential data is another data type, used in manufacturing, reducing duplicates in data. A comparison of both sequential data types in this context is not fully explored in the literature. This paper explores a set of experiments to evaluate both sequential data types using various ML methods and windowing mechanisms on a real-world manufacturing system. Based on the results, recommendations for practitioners are derived and an outlook to possible future investigation is given.

papers.title: Simulation and Finance: A Bibliometric Review
papers.summary: This study is a systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis of simulation in financial research. Journal articles and reviews indexed in Scopus and published between 2011 and 2026 were retrieved and screened using the PRISMA framework, giving a final sample of 3,704 records. Performance analysis and science mapping were carried out in Bibliometrix and Biblioshiny, and keyword co-occurrence was mapped in VOSviewer. The 2026 literature alone contains 405 publications, and keyword co-occurrence analysis identifies five clusters, of which three are examined in depth: finance, decentralised finance and behavioural decision-making; learning systems, prediction and simulation; and investment, risk and climate-linked simulation. Across the dataset, annual output grew at 8.65%, which points to a maturing rather than an explosive field. China and the United States produce the largest share of country output, and only 29.14% of authorships are international. The reviewed studies show that simulation can improve financial decision-making and test complex systems under varied conditions, but they rely heavily on small datasets, self-built models and assumptions that are rarely tested on live markets. The main gaps are the distance between simulated success and empirical verification, the separation of research streams, and the limited presence of emerging economies such as India.

papers.title: AI-Driven Data Supply Chain
papers.summary: This book explores the transformation of data management through AI-driven solutions, emphasizing the critical role of an intelligent and adaptive data supply chain. It covers essential topics such as AI-powered data discovery, automated data pipelines, data governance, and real-time analytics. The book also examines practical applications, including cost optimization in cloud environments, security and privacy considerations, and real-world case studies. Key features: Defines a new data foundation based on the concept of a data supply chain and bridges the gap between theory and implementation through AI-driven approaches. Promotes the development of a comprehensive Data and AI ecosystem. Presents a focused blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, supported by hands-on examples and step-by-step frameworks. Focuses on AI-powered data lifecycle management, with automation and visibility at its core. Applies the shift-left principle by embedding Generative AI into data foundation practices, proposing and implementing innovative and improved methodologies. This book is intended for data professionals, AI practitioners, IT managers, business analysts, senior executives, product managers, and academics specializing in data science and supply chain management.
